topics.title: Threats and prevention; viruses, worms, ransomware and Trojans

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish a virus from a worm by how each needs a host and how each replicates.
Explain how ransomware holds user data hostage and how a Trojan disguises itself as legitimate software.
Describe how spyware collects user information secretly and how adware earns revenue through advertisements.
Explain the threat of keyloggers and why an online virtual keyboard resists them better than an on-screen keyboard.

topics.title: Modes of malware distribution and combating malware

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the common routes by which malware reaches a computer.
Recognise signs of malware infection and choose suitable preventive measures.
Compare signature-based, sandbox, data mining, heuristic and real-time methods of malware identification.
Explain what email spam is and how spam filtering and user marking help.
Compare HTTP and HTTPS in terms of encryption and suitable uses.
Explain how a firewall filters traffic using rules and distinguish network and host-based firewalls.

topics.title: Cookies and threats due to cookies

concepts.learning_objective: Describe what a cookie is and the roles of session and authentication cookies.
Identify threats from supercookies, zombie cookies and third-party tracking cookies.
Explain the role of white hat (ethical) hackers in securing systems.
Classify hackers as white, black or grey hats (and hacktivists) based on their intent.
Explain DoS and DDoS attacks and why DDoS is harder to counter.
Identify intrusion attacks such as asymmetric routing, buffer overflow and traffic flooding.
